raw_response:
I have farmed these 5 mu in Quzhou for 33 years, and I know what works on this land. My household has seven people, and with some of them working off-farm, I need to be careful with labor — I cannot do everything by hand, and I must time things right. I have a well, so water is not my biggest worry, but electricity for the pump costs money, so I do not waste irrigation.

For wheat, I always rotary till before sowing in October. I buy improved wheat seeds from the county supply shop — varieties like Jimai 22 that my neighbors grow too, because they are reliable. I spread compound fertilizer as base dressing before sowing, and at the jointing stage I topdress with urea. I irrigate three times: once to ensure good emergence, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I spray herbicide early, and I spray for insects and disease twice more before harvest. If the weather is normal, I should get about 500 kg per mu.

For maize, the season is short after wheat harvest in June. I plant hybrid seeds directly into the wheat stubble without tillage — there is no time to plow, and anyway the soil is fine like this. I apply fertilizer at sowing and topdress with urea at the big trumpet stage. I irrigate twice: once if it is dry right after sowing, and once during flowering or grain filling. I spray herbicide once and insecticide once for corn borer. I expect about 550 kg per mu in a normal year.
